topicName: Query Store: Capture, Analysis, and Plan Forcing
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Query Store - Capture, Analysis, and Plan Forcing in Microsoft SQL Server"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Query Store functions as a time machine for your SQL Server database. By continuously capturing execution plans, runtime statistics, and query text, it helps Database Administrators (DBAs) isolate performance regressions caused by plan changes. This tutorial covers configuring data capture, analyzing performance, and using plan forcing to resolve regressions."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"1. Enabling and Configuring Query Store"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before using Query Store, it must be enabled on your user databases. You can enable it via SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) or T-SQL."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"ALTER DATABASE YourDatabaseName SET QUERY_STORE = ON (
    OPERATION_MODE = READ_WRITE,
    CLEANUP_POLICY = (STALE_QUERY_THRESHOLD_DAYS = 30),
    DATA_FLUSH_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 900,
    INTERVAL_LENGTH_MINUTES = 60,
    MAX_STORAGE_SIZE_MB = 1024,
    QUERY_CAPTURE_MODE = AUTO
);"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"OPERATION_MODE: Sets Query Store to read/write mode to actively capture data."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"QUERY_CAPTURE_MODE = AUTO: Automatically filters out trivial and infrequent queries to save space."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"MAX_STORAGE_SIZE_MB: Defines the maximum space Query Store can consume before triggering internal cleanup."},{"order":9,"type":"heading","text":"2. Analyzing Performance Regressions"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once data is captured, you can identify queries that experienced performance regressions using built-in SSMS reports or T-SQL queries."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"SELECT 
    T.query_sql_text,
    Q.query_id,
    P.plan_id,
    D.max_duration / 1000 AS max_duration_ms,
    D.avg_duration / 1000 AS avg_duration_ms
FROM sys.query_store_query_text AS T
JOIN sys.query_store_query AS Q ON T.query_text_id = Q.query_text_id
JOIN sys.query_store_plan AS P ON Q.query_id = P.query_id
JOIN sys.query_store_runtime_stats AS RS ON P.plan_id = RS.plan_id
JOIN sys.query_store_runtime_stats_interval AS RSI ON RS.runtime_stats_interval_id = RSI.runtime_stats_interval_id
WHERE RSI.start_time >= DATEADD(day, -7, GETDATE())
ORDER BY avg_duration_ms DESC;"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can also view the 'Regressed Queries' report directly in SSMS by expanding your database in Object Explorer, navigating to Query Store, and selecting Regressed Queries."},{"order":13,"type":"heading","text":"3. Forcing Execution Plans"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"If a query regression is caused by a sub-optimal execution plan chosen by the optimizer, you can manually force a known good plan using Query Store."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"EXEC sp_query_store_force_plan 
    @query_id = 42, 
    @plan_id = 15;"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"To verify that the plan was successfully forced, query the sys.query_store_plan catalog view."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"SELECT 
    query_id,
    plan_id,
    is_forced_plan,
    force_failure_count,
    last_force_failure_reason_desc
FROM sys.query_store_plan
WHERE query_id = 42;"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"If you need to revert the forced plan and allow the optimizer to choose dynamically again, use the unforce stored procedure."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"EXEC sp_query_store_unforce_plan 
    @query_id = 42, 
    @plan_id = 15;"},{"order":20,"type":"heading","text":"Summary"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Query Store removes the guesswork from performance tuning. By enabling capture mode, analyzing historical metrics, and forcing stable execution plans, you can maintain consistent application performance in Microsoft SQL Server."}]
